description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates how the absolute mean (“Abs Mean”) of hidden states varies across model layers for three conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Layer” on a linear scale, spanning approximately 0 to 23 with tick labels shown at regular 5-layer intervals (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean” on a linear scale, ranging from about 0 up to a little above 4 (top visible values around 4.4), with numeric ticks at integer values. Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line labeled “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71,” which starts near 0 at layer 0, rises to around 0.2 by roughly layers 2–3, stays around ~0.2–0.4 through the mid layers, increases to about ~0.9 near layer 19, then jumps sharply to roughly ~2.6 around layer 21 and ends near ~4.4 at the final layer; an orange dotted line labeled “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05,” which stays close to 0 across layers, gradually increasing from near 0 at early layers to around ~0.05–0.1 by the last layers with a small dip visible around the low 20s; and a green solid line labeled “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04,” which also remains near 0 throughout, slowly increasing from near 0 at layer 0 to roughly ~0.08–0.1 by the final layer without sharp spikes.
